coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: MOLSW Notice 3534/MLSF (27 Sep 2024, effective 1 Oct 2024) sets a LAK 2.5m/month minimum total pay incl. subsistence allowance for low-paid employees, explicitly including household employees. A 2022 MOLSW decision on managing and inspecting domestic-worker employers is mentioned in secondary text (unverified; could not locate text). No household-employer registration regime found. Social Security Law 2018: employer 6%, employee 5.5%, cap LAK 4.5m; PwC says government encourages even 1-employee enterprises to register; ILO/LSSO Feb 2026 workshop plans to link social-security registration to sectoral licensing.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: One search returned only non-Lao results; no Lao scrap-metal licence or register found. Not verified either way.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K03 (pawnshop). No separate second-hand dealer regime found (not searched separately).

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: No gold-shop licence found. AML Law 49/NA (2015) lists antique and precious-metal dealers as reporting units: customer ID checks, report within 3 days of transactions above BOL-set thresholds or suspicious ones. Thresholds not found.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler or parts-shop licence found. MOIC Notice 1662 (5 Jul 2024) paused new vehicle import-export business licences until 1 Jan 2025; a 2026 report says new petrol/diesel passenger-vehicle imports are suspended 1 Jun 2026 to end-2026 (used-car coverage unclear). Nothing buildable found.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Decree 644 (animal movement, import/export/transit) and Decision 0795/MAF need DLF permits and health certificates; Technical Norms on livestock apply to anyone doing livestock business. No livestock-market licence or domestic movement-permit digital system found.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Slaughterhouse establishment licence (DLF, 12-month validity, site inspections; datasheet 2017) and Decree 516 on slaughter and meat hygiene inspection. No butcher-retail licence found.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Nothing found: beekeeping undeveloped, no registration regime or register duty found.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Licences for animal health clinics (MoAF-LFD-10) and animal pharmacy/equipment shops (MoAF-LFD-11), both DLF, in-person. Decree on veterinary medicines requires business registration with DLF; 2024 notification required producers, importers and distributors of feed and vet medicine to register before 30 Jun 2024.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: MONRE Decision 1509 on underground water (permits for drilling and use, small/medium/large scales; date unverified) and a ministerial decision authorising officials to regulate the well-drilling business (undated). No reporting scheme found.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Only a Savannakhet provincial faecal-sludge regulation (SNV, 2016) requiring vacuum-truck operators to register; WEPA says no national guideline and sludge treatment exists only in Vientiane. No national regime.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: A Lao Trade Portal regulation covers 'special equipment' (boilers, pressure vessels, lifts, escalators, amusement facilities, hazardous tanks) with standard certification via a National Standard Certification and Investigation Centre and licences for installers; decree number and date not found, periodic-inspection duties unconfirmed.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Nam Papa (urban piped water, MPWT) and Nam Saat (rural water, MoH) are state-run; ADB/JICA projects dominate. No private small-water-system licence found.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Decree on Pesticide Management 258/GoL (24 Aug 2017) and MAF Decision 0238/MAF (14 Feb 2019) on pesticide business operation; product registration with DoA (MoAF-DoA-5). MAF Order 2592/MOAF (2014) covers fertiliser, seed and pesticide. Dealer licence article text not retrieved; annual-report duty not found.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K02. Context: 2024 revision of job-placement law and decree on dispatching Lao workers; MOLSW monitors about 30 agencies via an online system; Thailand MOU 2016 (amended later, undated).

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No Lao cemetery, crematorium or funeral licence found; deaths registered at district Home Affairs office; funerals largely temple-based. Nothing found.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Decree 238 (2017) on Associations: MOHA registration valid one year, annual renewal, annual reports, donations over LAK 50m reported to Ministry of Finance; religious bodies excluded; no 2025 replacement found. Halal/kosher not applicable.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi licence and passenger-transport licence (MPWT; passenger transport needs LAK 1bn capital, at least 5 vehicles, Lao-only; datasheets 2018). District offices handle vehicle registration, technical inspection and driving tests (Vientiane Times Jan 2024). Freight-operator guidelines exist (Tilleke). No tuk-tuk or moto-taxi regime found.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money changers: licence needs LAK 1bn capital; bureaus had to become agents of commercial banks by 11 Oct 2021; Decision 449 (Jun 2022) limits them to buying FX from individuals with a daily cap equal to registered equity, and sales to individuals up to LAK 15m per person per day. Vendors: Vientiane relocation of street vendors (2024 report), Luang Namtha weekly market trial 2026 (fees waived in trial), border-market Decision 0807. No national vendor register.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Private Education Decree 332/GOV (19 Jul 2024, gazetted 30 Sep 2024) replaces Decree 64/PM of 1995; establishment licence from education and sports authority after enterprise registration. Food: Food Law 04/NA (2004), Decision 297/MOH (2012) on food inspection (street vending excluded), FDD product registration for permitted food producers. No driving-school or tattoo rules found; hunting outfitters not applicable (searches not spent).

candidates.buyer: Smallholder coffee cooperatives, village collectors, small processors and exporters on the Bolaven Plateau and in Sekong and Xieng Khouang, selling directly or via Vietnam/Thailand to EU buyers
candidates.category: 22. Commodity traders / 30. Exporters with traceability rules
candidates.evidence: https://efi.int/article/lao-pdr-and-eudr-new-reports-identify-practical-pathways-coffee-sector-preparedness ; https://efi.int/publication/preparedness-check-lao-coffee-eu-deforestation-regulation ; https://www.eeas.europa.eu/delegations/lao-pdr/eu-deforestation-regulation-%E2%80%93-eu-declares-laos-%E2%80%9Clow-risk%E2%80%9D_en . Direct EU exports are about 13% of Lao coffee exports; Vietnam about 53% and Thailand about 17%; about 100,000 livelihoods. EFI lists plot geolocation, traceability systems and legality documents as gaps; no Lao national platform named.
candidates.existing: Lao-language competitor search found no Lao-specific app. Generic tools exist: TechnoServe TerraTrac (free Android app), Fairtrade Plot Insights, TraceX. No Lao deployment of any of them was found. Donor projects (EFI/EU, GIZ) may supply free tools.
candidates.known_note: Same type of export-compliance record as K01 but a different crop, buyer group and market (EU, not China).
candidates.name: Lao coffee cooperative/trader EUDR plot-geolocation and due-diligence data pack
candidates.trigger: EUDR main obligations from 30 Dec 2026 (micro/small operators by 30 Jun 2027 under the Dec 2025 amendment). Farm-level traceability, plot geolocation (polygons above 4 ha) and legality documents are expected even for low-risk Laos.
candidates.unchecked: Whether buyers (Vietnamese/Thai roasters, Lao exporters) will pay or push the tool; whether donor projects are already giving cooperatives free tools; number of Lao coffee cooperatives and exporters; Lao-language usability; connectivity in the highlands.

candidates.unchecked: Whether filings are paper, email or an online system; how many small inbound agencies; the effective date and any Lao-language official notice; competitor search in Lao (local-language search not run, which is needed if this is scored 3 or more).

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Retail station licence valid 2 years, renewable (MoIC Decision 1806/2009 conditions; one brand per station); 2026 fuel shortages, closed stations and state-funds committee (KPL, Mar 2026); ministry sets national retail prices (adjustments June and Sept 2026). No e-invoice, stock-reporting or LPG-specific rule found. Weak lead only.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Lao coffee EUDR readiness (EFI reports Jul/Aug 2026): obligations from 30 Dec 2026, micro/small operators to 30 Jun 2027; Laos rated low risk; smallholder cooperatives lack plot geolocation and traceability; no Lao national tool named. Candidate C1.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: No 2024-2025 decree on savings/credit unions or reporting forms found; BOL regulation on savings and credit unions exists but its text was not reached. Related finding: BOL paused new microfinance and pawnshop licences in Vientiane on 31 Jul 2026, with a revised framework due around Nov 2026 (see K03). Decree 184/G (2022) on microfinance, 2-year transition ended around Jul 2024.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Nothing new for clinic licensing or insurer billing. Adjacent: MOH Decision 3730 (biopharma/stem cells, in force Jan 2025); medical-device registration Decision 1470/MOH; FDD online drug registration mandatory since 1 Jan 2026 (manufacturer/importer side, not clinics). No clinic reporting duty found.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Retail pharmacy licence by FDD, fee by type (1-3) per 2 years, Type 3 renewed by provincial health dept (2017 trade-portal datasheet; may be outdated). FDD online system covers drug registration only, per sources seen. Controlled-chemical users not reached. Weak candidate C5, unverified.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: No security/cleaning agency licensing rule found. Labour: Decree 245 (2020) on placing Lao workers abroad being aligned with 2023 Employment Law (2025 process) (K02 area); labour ministry suspended entry/employment of Bangladeshi workers from 1 Sept until end-2026; Labour Welfare Fund contributions (0.25% each) start 1 Oct 2026.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Lao-language contractor-registration search returned only irrelevant foreign results. Mining: PM Order 06/2025 (7 Mar 2025) permanently bans alluvial gold extraction and suction dredging, suspends new metallic mineral approvals, and moves trial mining to regular licensing. This is mostly enforcement, with no small-firm recurring reporting workflow found. Small-scale royalty return rules not found.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Search returned nothing Laos-specific on DNFBP/AML reporting (AMLIO, APG and FATF pages not reached). Unverifiable in this pass.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Hotel/guesthouse licence is annual and Lao-owned only for guesthouses (2018 trade-portal datasheet). Tourism Police notice of 12 May 2026: inbound tour companies must attach confirmed hotel bookings for every night; the stated goal is to digitise tourist accommodation records. LAK 10,000 tourism fee collected electronically at borders. Online arrival registration (immigration) mandatory from 1 Sep 2025 and asks for stay address. No direct hotel guest-register e-reporting duty confirmed. Candidates C3 and C6.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: EUDR for coffee, timber and rubber (see category 22). EU delegation says outputs must be traceable at farm level even though Laos is low risk. No Lao government traceability certificate found. K01 (durian/China) is a different crop and market.

coverage.category: 31. Online sellers and e-commerce operators (MoIC e-commerce registration)
coverage.found: Decree 296/GOV (2021) requires operators to notify or register with MoIC. Notice 3988 (17 Dec 2025, effective 1 Feb 2026) launched the free E-Trust app for certificates and licences, with paper still allowed. Decision 2828/MOIC (11 Nov 2025) sets fines. The state app covers the filing, so this is a weak lead (C2).

coverage.category: 32. Inbound tour operators and guides (Tourism Police group-entry filings)
coverage.found: Per-group submission of passenger lists, passports, itineraries, checkpoints, hotels and guides to Tourism Police; hotel booking confirmations for every night added by 12 May 2026 notice. Frequent mandatory filing by small agencies. Candidate C3.

coverage.category: 33. Microfinance institutions and pawnshops (BOL licensing)
coverage.found: BOL suspended new MFI and pawnshop licences in Vientiane (31 Jul 2026); applications expected to reopen in Nov 2026 under stricter rules; existing licensees keep operating; provinces unaffected. Related to K03.

coverage.category: 34. Mining and quarry licensing, alluvial gold and sand
coverage.found: See category 27. PM Order 06/2025 is mostly a ban and enforcement, so it is not a software workflow.

coverage.category: 35. Crypto mining and digital-asset operators
coverage.found: Rules reportedly require resident ownership, USD 5m deposit and a 10 MW minimum (unverified summary), and power cut-off was planned for early 2026. Only large firms are affected, so it is out of scope.

coverage.category: 36. Employer social security, Labour Welfare Fund and foreign-worker duties
coverage.found: Labour Welfare Fund 0.25% employer and 0.25% employee contributions from 1 Oct 2026 (rising to 0.5% from 1 Oct 2031); Social Security Law Arts. 34 and 38 revised in 2025; foreign-worker employer advertising rules relaxed. This is generic payroll and mostly out of scope. Weak C4.

coverage.category: 37. Inbound tourist online arrival registration (immigration)
coverage.found: Online arrival registration pilot 15 Aug 2025, mandatory from 1 Sep 2025 at 4 international checkpoints, with address of stay required. It falls on travellers and tour firms. Hotel angle only; no separate candidate.

result.competitor: The core job is already covered by free tools, and the strongest is donor-backed. EFI, the same body running the Lao coffee EUDR preparedness work (Technical Facility running 2024-2028), offers WHIMO ("What is My Origin"), launched Feb 2026. It is free and open source, and is built to let cooperatives, aggregators, processors and exporters record farm geodata and transactions in low-infrastructure settings. Fairtrade Plot Insights is free for Fairtrade-certified cooperatives. It does polygon upload, quality checks, deforestation analysis and GeoJSON export for TRACES. The Fairtrade NAPP project covers Lao producer organisations. TechnoServe TerraTrac is a free app. PT Koltiva, a traceability vendor, took part in a 2026 Indonesia-Laos coffee programme on digital traceability in Huaphan. Large buyers in Vietnam and Thailand usually run their own supplier mapping. I did not confirm an actual WHIMO or Plot Insights rollout in Laos.
result.duty: The obligation is real but indirect, and it is not Lao law. EUDR (Reg. 2023/1115 as amended by Reg. 2025/2650, in force 26 Dec 2025) applies to EU operators and traders from 30 Dec 2026, and from 30 Jun 2027 for micro and small operators. Those operators must hold plot geolocation (polygons above 4 ha), legality evidence and a due-diligence statement. Lao cooperatives and exporters only need this data because EU buyers contractually require it. Most Lao coffee goes to Vietnam (about 53%) and Thailand (about 17%), and only re-exports to the EU are affected. Laos is rated low risk, so simplified due diligence applies, but geolocation is still required. Penalties fall on the EU operator. For Lao sellers the risk is losing market access, not a fine. There is no recurring filing with a Lao authority. The data pack is supplied per shipment or per season.
result.market: The market is very small. The Lao Coffee Association has about 65 members, including 6 cooperatives covering about 3,450 households (Lao Trade Portal, ILO). The largest cooperative, CPC Bolaven, has about 484 households under a 2026 KPL report. Coffee exports were about USD 89.9M in 2021, and about 100,000 livelihoods depend on coffee. Direct EU exports are only about 13% of the total. The likely paying buyers are a few dozen cooperatives and exporters at most.
result.reason: The EUDR is in force, but it binds EU operators, not Lao businesses, and only about 13% of Lao coffee goes directly to the EU. Free tools already do the core job of capturing polygons, keeping traceability records and exporting GeoJSON. EFI's WHIMO is the main one: it is free and open source, aimed at cooperatives and exporters, and comes from the same donor running the Lao coffee EUDR work. Fairtrade Plot Insights is also free, and TerraTrac is free too. A traceability vendor (Koltiva) is already active in Lao coffee training. The market is tiny: about 65 association members and 6 major cooperatives, with donor-subsidised expectations. Willingness to pay is low, and Lao-language support and highland connectivity add cost. One weakness in this check: I found no confirmed Lao deployment of WHIMO or Plot Insights. Even so, a solo founder would struggle to compete with free donor tools.
